purpose: Regression for the automatic nuclear detection scale (nuclear-size/1.1.0): a field whose nuclear channel carries a large-scale background brighter than the nuclear contrast. Under nuclear-size/1.0.0 the estimate is about ten times the nucleus diameter and StarDist returns one nucleus for the field.
attribution: Images: Schmidt HB, Rohatgi R, Brandman O (2022), DS6b_5EU_TimeCourse_RawData, Zenodo, doi:10.5281/zenodo.6643490, CC BY 4.0. Cropped, one channel; pixel values unchanged.
citation: Schmidt HB et al. Oxaliplatin disrupts nucleolar function through biophysical disintegration. Cell Reports 2022. doi:10.1016/j.celrep.2022.111629

ds6b-30min-cis100-294-nuclear-640.tif.channel: OME channel 0 (filter DAPI, NucBlue / Hoechst 33342), uint16, 0.325 um/px
ds6b-30min-cis100-294-nuclear-640.tif.modifications: Top-left 640 x 640 pixels of the nuclear plane; zlib-compressed TIFF; pixel values unchanged.
ds6b-30min-cis100-294-nuclear-640.tif.selection: One of the 11 DS6b tuning fields whose nuclear detection broke in the public nucleolar validation (docs/public-nucleolar-shape-validation.md). The crop was chosen because nuclear-size/1.0.0 still fails on it (estimated diameter 572 px; nuclei in this field are about 50-90 px).
